written: That logic felt airtight. Second opinion: my desktop. It boots, the card's fans spin, and Windows never sees it. Card two: identical. Two dead cards! I wrote the return ticket. One last try, with the power supply's own cable instead of the adapter. It boots! The card shows up, healthy! The adapter was the problem the whole time. Of course, my power supply's maker said so. written: From my SSD it takes about three minutes, because the SSD is the slow part, not the slot. The model is Fish Audio Drama 3: thirty-six billion parameters, but only about three billion work for each slice of sound. Squeezed to four bits, it fits on one card. What broke: the server's disk corrupted a weight file, a stale library path crashed the compiler, and a faster setting for the expert math filled a layer with garbage, so it stayed off.

written: Day one: the original model on the CPU, one layer at a time, as a reference. Day two: every weight mapped and checked against it. On day three, the first eight test lines took fourteen point seven seconds for every second of speech. What worked: one traced pass through the network for every frame, the audio decoder in a single trace, sampling on the card, a cached voice prompt, and the codec on the card as well. I kept the four-bit weights, and by the end of day four the card needed zero point eight five seconds for every second of speech.
